Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
ho...@intergate.bc.ca (Michal Kranc) writes:

>Q: If i block a vampire with an ACHING BEUTY on it and he plays CHANGE
>OF TARGET do i still loose the 1 pool for blocking .

Yes. CoT is played after the block. So the blocker would already have
cost the controlling Meth a pool.

>Q: When my prey yelds a contestion when do i get my card back ?

During your next untap phase.

>Q: What is the final ruling on the TOMB OF RAMSES

Play as written. No ruling has been given.

>Q: Can you put more blood on an uncontrolled vampire then it's capacity
>is ?

Yes. It will come out at the end of the influence phase of its would-be
controller (if it still has sufficient blood on it at that time). The
excess will then drain off to the blood bank, as normal.

>Does it immediately drain off? I thought it only drains off when the vamp
>becomes controlled. So if that is indeed the case and you still have some
>transfers left, you should be able to pull the additional blood back.

It does not immediately drain off.

It only drains off when the vampire becomes controlled.

The vamp will (mandatorily) become controlled at the end of the
influence phase, if he still has blood on him equal to or in
excess of his capacity.

You could use transfers to pull some blood off of him before that
time, true.

>text "breaks the rules" and allows over-capacity vamps. Of course, the

The third is unlikely, I'll grant you. Issuing errata is typically not
done in parenthesis within a post regarding a different issue.

A fourth (and the actual) reason is: he said "or greater" because that's
the way the game's played - no errata necessary. He put it in parenthesis
because it was just reminder text as to what "enough blood on them" means.

Here's a better example from my archives - a little less questionable:

From: aa...@cats.ucsc.edu (Thomas R Wylie)

Newsgroups: rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad
Subject: Re: Influence/Transfers (was Re: Some questions...)
Date: 19 Jan 1995 04:07:55 GMT
Message-ID: <3fkoir$f...@darkstar.UCSC.EDU>

You can always give a vampire more blood than its capacity. If the
vampire is controlled, the excess immediately, well, bleeds off
(except in the case of Steal Blood, when the excess is used to heal
damage for the rest of the combat, and then any excess goes away).
If the vampire is uncontrolled, it simply pops out at the end of the
influence phase, and immediately bleeds off any excess; this gives you
time to draw the excess into your pool via transfers.

>>damage? I like this very much, but was unaware of the change. When was
>>this reversed?

>I cannot find a reference for it being reversed

I think I've found the thread of my reasoning.

The exception existed in the Jyhad rulebook:

[15.3]
If the amount stolen exceeds the stealing vampire's capacity, the excess
is kept on the vampire until the end of the turn and then put in the bank.

None of the examples in the Jyhad rulebook illustrate this point, however.

The exception was clearly eliminated in the VtES rulebook:

(8.3)
If the stolen blood exceeds the capacity of the vampire stealing it,
the excess is moved to the blood bank

This rule is illustrated in an example:

(21.1)
The attack steals 2 blood. Eliza steals one point to go up
to full capacity. She can't steal the second blood point, however, because
she's now at full blood capacity. Cassandra still loses 2 blood, however,
and the extra blood point goes into the blood bank

And it goes on to say (unrelated to the fact that the excess drains off
immediately):

The stolen blood will also heal the vampire immediately. This blood can be
burned by damage that is not dealt with First Strike.

(Illustrating the point that blood is burned to heal damage /after/ the
strikes are resolved).

This last bit can cause confusion if read too quickly. It can (and often
is) misinterpretted to mean something akin to the Jyhad rule.

The outline (version 2.0) was updated to reflect this new rule, as presented
in the post by Tom Wylie of 28 Sep 1995 - a post which came compete with
all of the errata to the rulebook. That errata did not include any changes
to the Steal Blood rule.

Except for an off-hand reference from Tom in Feb 1996, no other official
mention of the rule has been made. At the time, I did not take Tom's
reference as an attempt to issue new errata, but rather just ruling based
on what Tom viewed as existing errata. I could be wrong in this belief,
but that's how I read the article.

This off-hand reference was probably (IMHO) in error, much as Tom's
short-lived assertion that a stolen weapon could be used the same
round in which it was stolen if the thief had additional strikes.

I would recommend, for people who use official rules (like JOL, and
some other groups), that the rules as printed in the VtES rulebook
be taken as official.

For the majority of groups out there that use house rules to make the
game work, I present my reasoning here and suggest that you discuss it
during your next session, before it actually comes up in play.

Happy hunting...


